skills.description: Runs a pre-launch legal and policy audit over an app or website codebase: policies matched against what the code actually does, consent and data discipline, honesty in marketing and pricing, accessibility basics, and asset rights — audit first with evidence, then fixes one item at a time. Explicitly not legal advice: uncertain items go on a "take to a lawyer" list and penalty figures are never invented.

skills.name: design-system
skills.title: Design System
skills.description: Design-token architecture (primitive to semantic to component), component specs, and brand-compliant slides.

skills.name: diagram-design
skills.title: diagram-design

skills.name: draw-icons
skills.title: Draw Icons

skills.name: emil-design-eng
skills.title: emil-design-eng

skills.name: fontshare
skills.title: Fontshare

Always check license_type per family before use; never vendor FFL files.
skills.license: Mixed: ITF Free Font License (64) + SIL OFL (36)

skills.name: gsap-core
skills.title: gsap-core
skills.description: The official GreenSock skill for the GSAP core API: tweens, easing, stagger, defaults and matchMedia for responsive, reduced-motion-safe animation.
skills.why: GSAP is the web's reference animation engine and this is the vendor's own correct-usage layer — the base the other seven GSAP skills in this set build on.

skills.name: gsap-frameworks
skills.title: gsap-frameworks
skills.description: The official GreenSock skill for GSAP in Vue, Nuxt, Svelte and SvelteKit: lifecycle integration, scoped selectors and unmount cleanup.
skills.why: The non-React half of framework animation, straight from the vendor — completes the set for any frontend stack.

skills.name: gsap-performance
skills.title: gsap-performance
skills.description: The official GreenSock skill for animation performance: transform-first animation, avoiding layout thrash, will-change and batching for a stable 60fps.
skills.why: Jank is what makes animated sites feel cheap; this is the performance discipline behind smooth motion.

skills.name: gsap-plugins
skills.title: gsap-plugins
skills.description: The official GreenSock skill for the GSAP plugin ecosystem: registration, Flip, Draggable, SplitText, ScrollTo, ScrollSmoother, SVG and physics plugins.
skills.why: Half of GSAP's power lives in its plugins; this is the vendor's map of which plugin solves which motion problem.

skills.name: gsap-react
skills.title: gsap-react
skills.description: The official GreenSock skill for GSAP in React and Next.js: the useGSAP hook, refs, context scoping and cleanup on unmount.
skills.why: React is where GSAP most often leaks or double-fires; the vendor's own pattern prevents the classic bugs.

skills.name: gsap-scrolltrigger
skills.title: gsap-scrolltrigger
skills.description: The official GreenSock skill for ScrollTrigger: scroll-linked animation, pinning, scrub and parallax done right.
skills.why: Scroll-driven pages are the owner's site style (CV, donate page, this collection's own site); ScrollTrigger is the standard tool — and the easiest one to misuse.

skills.name: gsap-timeline
skills.title: gsap-timeline
skills.description: The official GreenSock skill for GSAP timelines: sequencing, the position parameter, nesting and playback control.
skills.why: Choreography is where hand-rolled animation falls apart; timelines are GSAP's core advantage, and this teaches them properly.

skills.name: gsap-utils
skills.title: gsap-utils
skills.description: The official GreenSock skill for gsap.utils: clamp, mapRange, interpolate, random, snap, wrap and pipe helpers.
skills.why: The small utility layer that keeps animation math declarative instead of hand-rolled.

skills.name: impeccable
skills.title: impeccable

Runtime note: its launcher downloads the design engine binary from the project's own GitHub releases, SHA-256-verified against the manifest vendored in the skill; the per-edit detector hook is opt-in per project.
skills.why: The design shelf's heavyweight: a design director's full command set plus a mechanical detector that catches slop after every edit — the closest thing to a standing design review in the collection.

skills.name: kubai-icons
skills.title: kubai-icons

skills.why: Icon generation in a single consistent style is a job no other design entry does — ui-ux-pro-max's data covers icon selection, not creation. Listed link-only: the skill's own license is source-available, bars translation and modified redistribution, and its text is Chinese, so it cannot be vendored into this English collection.

skills.name: slides
skills.title: Slides
skills.description: Creates strategic HTML presentations with charts, design tokens, and responsive layouts.
skills.why: Turns briefs and reports into presentable decks without design software.

skills.name: stageshow
skills.title: stageshow

React and plain CSS.

skills.name: domain-modeling

skills.name: durable-objects
skills.title: durable-objects
skills.description: Build, debug, or review Cloudflare Durable Objects code for persistent state and coordination.

skills.name: eval-harness
skills.title: eval-harness
skills.description: Eval-driven development for AI agent work: capability and regression evals defined before coding, code/model/rule/human graders, and pass@k / pass^k reliability tracking. Vendored as-is from ECC, where it is framed for Claude Code sessions; the methodology is harness-agnostic.
skills.why: The collection had zero eval methodology for prompt or agent changes — the exact gap behind flagship-validation failures in the owner's bots, where a change ships on vibes instead of a regression suite.

skills.name: executing-plans
skills.title: executing-plans

For when the human chose inline execution or no subagent tool exists.
skills.why: writing-plans produces the plan and SDD executes it with subagents; this is the inline path for harnesses without subagents — the same ledger discipline, with no fabricated dispatches.

skills.name: fast-anything
skills.title: fast-anything

skills.why: The first performance skill in the collection: a measured, verified hot-path port with a strong equivalence guarantee, instead of a full rewrite or blind optimisation.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.title: find-skills
skills.description: Finds and installs agent skills from the open ecosystem through the Skills CLI and the skills.sh registry.
skills.why: Skill discovery is a different job from skill authoring — and the front door for growing this very collection.

skills.name: finishing-a-development-branch
skills.title: finishing-a-development-branch
skills.description: Decides how completed work integrates once implementation is done and tests pass: verify the suite, detect the environment, present merge / pull-request / keep / discard options, execute the choice, and clean up the worktree safely.
skills.why: Closes the loop the other workflow skills open — worktrees and plans get you to done; this makes the merge-or-discard decision explicit and the cleanup safe instead of improvised.

skills.name: frameworks-on-cloudflare
skills.title: frameworks-on-cloudflare
skills.description: Build, migrate, and deploy web-framework applications on Cloudflare Workers. Use when a framework project such as Astro, SvelteKit, React Router, TanStack Start, Nuxt, Hono, or a React or Vue SPA targets Cloudflare, or when a framework repository contains Workers deployment configuration.
skills.why: Framework apps on Workers (Astro, SvelteKit, React Router, TanStack, Nuxt, Hono, SPAs) — the deploy side his vercel-react-best-practices (code rules) doesn't cover.

skills.name: grill-me
skills.title: Grill Me
skills.description: A relentless one-question-at-a-time interview that stress-tests a plan or design until every branch of the decision tree is resolved.
skills.why: The sharp end of requirements work: it surfaces the decisions brainstorming leaves unmade, before they turn into rework.

skills.name: grilling
skills.title: Grilling
skills.description: The reusable interview engine behind grill-me: grills the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea, one question at a time.
skills.why: Grill-me is the session wrapper; this is the portable technique that other workflows can invoke on any decision.

skills.name: improve
skills.title: improve
skills.description: Survey any codebase as a senior advisor and produce prioritized, self-contained implementation plans for other models/agents to execute — read-only on source code, never implements anything itself.
skills.why: The audit-first advisor loop: recon, then a 9-category parallel audit, findings vetted and prioritized by leverage, and plans written for the weakest plausible executor, executed in an isolated worktree — distinct from writing-plans (plans from a given spec) and subagent-driven-development (executes an existing plan).

skills.name: mcp-builder
skills.title: mcp-builder
skills.description: Anthropic's playbook for designing and building high-quality MCP servers, with reference guides and an evaluation harness.
skills.why: The owner builds connectors and MCP-backed tools; this is the reference guide from the source.

skills.name: ponytail
skills.title: Ponytail
skills.description: Lazy senior-dev mode: the smallest change that fully solves the task, explained in one read.
skills.why: Cuts over-engineering, tokens, and cost on everyday coding without dropping safety or tests.

skills.name: ponytail-audit
skills.title: Ponytail Audit
skills.description: One-shot whole-repo audit for bugs, security holes, slow paths, untested risky code, and deletable bloat.
skills.why: A fast health check for inherited or fast-grown codebases, ranked by impact.

skills.name: ponytail-debt
skills.title: Ponytail Debt
skills.description: Lists every deliberate shortcut: marker in the code as a debt ledger.
skills.why: Keeps intentional shortcuts visible so they get repaid instead of forgotten.

skills.name: ponytail-review
skills.title: Ponytail Review
skills.description: Quality review of a change: correctness, safety, load behavior, tests, and whether every line earns its place.
skills.why: Catches risky or bloated diffs before they ship, explained in plain language.

skills.name: prompt-caching-strategy
skills.title: prompt-caching-strategy
skills.description: Restructuring prompts for cache reuse — stable prefix, dynamic suffix — with provider-aware guidance and honest treatment of unmeasured savings.
skills.why: Prompt size is the known biggest cost lever in the owner's bot fleet (established by his own audits) and nothing in the collection covered cache-oriented prompt structure.

skills.name: receiving-code-review
skills.title: receiving-code-review
skills.description: Receives code review feedback with technical rigor: verify each suggestion against the codebase before implementing it, push back with evidence when feedback is wrong, and never perform agreement or blindly implement.
skills.why: The underrated half of code review — it stops agents from cargo-culting reviewer suggestions and turns feedback into verified fixes instead of performative compliance.

skills.name: requesting-code-review
skills.title: requesting-code-review
skills.description: Requests a focused code review at the right moments — after tasks, major features, and before merging — dispatching a reviewer with a prompt template that checks the work against its requirements and plan.
skills.why: Pairs with receiving-code-review as the two halves of review discipline; the collection had review-adjacent skills but none for dispatching a requirements-focused review at merge time.

skills.name: skill-creator
skills.title: skill-creator
skills.description: Anthropic's guide and tooling for creating, evaluating, and iterating on agent skills, with eval and description-tuning scripts.
skills.why: This repo curates skills for a living; the official skill-authoring workflow belongs in it.

skills.name: skillevaluator
skills.title: skillevaluator
skills.description: Multi-tier framework for evaluating AI agent skills: quality gates with a 0-100 score, security scanning, harness compatibility checks, semantic overlap detection, synthetic eval datasets, and live agent A/B evaluation of skill lift — with reusable CI templates.
skills.why: Skill evaluation is a genuinely distinct, unoccupied cluster: no existing entry scores skill quality/security, detects semantic overlap between skills, or A/B-tests skill lift. Tier 1 runs keyless (no API key, GPU or Docker) and gives every skill a 0-100 quality score plus a security/PII scan — direct curation QA for a 121-skill collection — and Tier 2 overlap detection speaks to the one-skill-per-cluster rule. Honest limit: harness-check and Tier 3 live agents do NOT include Muse (agents: opencode, codex, claude-code), so with/without lift measured there is a proxy, not a measurement on Muse.

skills.name: strategic-compact
skills.title: Strategic Compact
skills.description: Suggests manual context compaction at logical task-phase boundaries, so long sessions compact deliberately instead of at arbitrary auto-compaction points.
skills.why: Long agent sessions die at context limits; compacting at phase boundaries keeps the working thread coherent across a whole build.
skills.adaptations: Ships a Claude Code-specific PreToolUse hook (suggest-compact.js); the compaction guidance itself is harness-portable.

skills.name: subagent-driven-development
skills.title: subagent-driven-development
skills.description: Executes an implementation plan with fresh subagents per task, with spec and quality review gates between tasks.
skills.why: The execution engine for writing-plans in multi-agent harnesses; how the owner's bigger builds actually get run.

skills.name: systematic-debugging
skills.title: systematic-debugging
skills.description: A root-cause-first debugging method: reproduce, isolate, and prove the cause before changing any code.
skills.why: Ends guess-and-patch debugging loops; pairs with this project's verify-against-real-behavior rule.

skills.name: test-driven-development
